rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /\b(patient handling|physiotherapy and occupational therapy|aids for daily living|wheelchairs?)\b/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on.
rules.suppliers: Every supplier NHS Supply Chain names on the frameworks above, resolved to one name per company through the Hub's alias registry, and ordered by how many of this speciality's frameworks they appear on. That count is the only claim made. It is not a ranking of size or share. Where NHS Supply Chain spelled a company two ways across its own pages, both spellings are shown against the one entry.
rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(patient handling|manual handling|moving and handling|people handling|hoists?|patient sling|hoist sling|toileting sling|standing sling|falls prevention|falls management|falls detection|fall detection|falls service|mobility (?:aids?|equipment|goods|services?|scooters?)|walking aid|walking frame|rollator|crutch(?:es)?|wheelchairs?|specialist seating|postural support|riser recliner|profiling bed|hospital beds?|bed rails?|mattress(?:es)?|pressure redistribut\w*|pressure relieving|pressure area care|patient transfer|transfer board|slide sheet|glide sheet|(?:integrated )?community equipment(?: service| loan\w*| framework)?|aids for daily living|daily living aids?|bariatric|stand(?:ing)? aids?|turning aid|stairlift|stair lift)\b/i and does not match /\b(wheelchair lifts?|b7r|disabled adaptations|atw grant|hcid)\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality. A CPV code beginning 33193 or 3319212 is recorded as corroboration where the feed carries one, but never admits a notice on its own: a notice carrying a basket of CPV codes is filed under all of them and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: No Drug Tariff part applies to this speciality. Part IX reimburses dressings and elastic hosiery (IXA), incontinence appliances (IXB), stoma appliances (IXC) and elastic hosiery (IXR); nothing on this patch is listed there, so the panel carries no tariff rather than reaching for the nearest part.
rules.directorySuppliers: Companies the Hub's own supplier directory files under this speciality, from the speciality labels on each company's directory record, resolved through speciality-label-map.json and speciality-map.json (Compare ids: handling). They are labelled DIRECTORY-TAGGED because the tag is the Hub's filing of a company's range, not a procurement record: being listed here is not evidence of a contract or of volume, and the list is not a census of the market. A company that is also on this speciality's own frameworks is listed once, with the framework-named suppliers, and marked as also directory-tagged. WHERE A COMPANY IS ON ANOTHER FRAMEWORK: where a directory-tagged company is named on an NHS Supply Chain framework that is not counted as this speciality's, it is still listed, with that framework named against it and linked, so it is not lost from the page. 9 of the 21 listed here carry such a note. Framework names and links come from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs as held in frameworks.json; an agreement the directory records from another buying organisation, such as an NHS Shared Business Services framework, is shown as the directory states it.
rules.gpPrescribing: No BNF section is mapped to this speciality, so no GP prescribing market is sized here rather than borrowing a neighbouring page's.
rules.mhraDsu: MHRA does not tag Drug Safety Updates to this area: no GOV.UK therapeutic-area facet maps to this speciality. That is a fact about how GOV.UK files them, not a finding that there are no safety updates relevant to it.

localIntel.title: Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling (2025/S 000-086469)
localIntel.fact: Runs 24 months from 9 March 2026 to 8 March 2028, with an option to extend for a further 24 months. 53 suppliers, 10 of them new, across three lots: Lot 1 beds, mattresses, pressure reducing products and manual handling equipment; Lot 2 managed service for beds and mattresses; Lot 3 rental and decontamination. 982 new products were added. NHS Supply Chain says products are clinically assured through its clinical evaluation process, which the page calls CaPA.
localIntel.use: The national route for mattresses and pressure-reducing products until at least March 2028. NHS Innovation Service guidance says new suppliers cannot be added to an agreed framework, so a supplier not on it should expect trust tenders, other frameworks and the re-let.

localIntel.title: NHS procurement frameworks (innovation guide)
localIntel.fact: States that new suppliers cannot be added to an agreed procurement framework, except a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). The Medical Technology DPS for Innovative Products (Innovation DPS) is open to innovations submitted to the NHS Innovation Service and accepted by NHS Supply Chain, or referred to NHS Supply Chain by the HIN (as the page names it), and the technology must meet national policy objectives and have a National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) recommendation. Its categories are orthopaedics, trauma and spine; ophthalmology; audiology; cardiology; interventional radiology; endourology; endoscopy; neuromodulation; perfusion; ablation; minimally invasive surgery; In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR) products and tests; and radiology. Pressure area care is not on that list.
localIntel.quote: New suppliers cannot be added to an agreed procurement framework, except the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS).
localIntel.use: The only route the page names for joining mid-term is a DPS, and the Innovation DPS categories it lists do not include pressure area care.

localIntel.org: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
localIntel.title: Lease of Mattresses (C468662)
localIntel.fact: Medstrom Ltd was awarded a seven-year lease of mattresses, pumps and cushions, £900,320.05 excluding VAT, with the award criterion given as price and one tender received. The notice records the procedure as award without prior publication, citing extreme urgency, and explains that the trust chose the supplier because the products are compatible with the trust's own products, as a direct award under the HTE framework (as the notice names it). It also says this is not a capital purchase: invoices are paid annually.
localIntel.quote: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust will be leasing these products over a 7 year period.
localIntel.use: Lease rather than capital, and compatibility with the trust's current beds is the stated reason. Seven years is a long commitment, and bed compatibility is the first objection a new support surface will meet.

localIntel.title: Bed Frames, Therapeutic Mattresses & Cushions
localIntel.fact: Call-off from a framework agreement awarded to Arjo UK Limited for the supply of bed frames, therapeutic mattresses and cushions for pressure relief, £928,290 (VAT basis not stated), running 1 August 2025 to 31 January 2027. The notice does not name the framework.
localIntel.quote: Supply of Bed Frames, Therapeutic Mattresses & Cushions pressure relief

localIntel.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
localIntel.title: Pressure ulcers: prevention and management (CG179)
localIntel.fact: Covers risk assessment, prevention and treatment for children, young people and adults at risk of, or with, a pressure ulcer, in secondary and tertiary care and in primary care, community care and emergency departments. On mattresses its recommendations say: use a high-specification foam mattress for adults admitted to secondary care or assessed as high risk in primary and community care (1.1.13); for adults with a pressure ulcer, use high-specification foam and, if that is not sufficient to redistribute pressure, consider a dynamic support surface (1.4.9); do not use standard-specification foam for adults with a pressure ulcer (1.4.10). Adults at high risk should change position at least every 4 hours (1.1.9). NICE last reviewed the guideline on 30 November 2018 and found no new evidence affecting the recommendations.
localIntel.quote: We have found no new evidence that affects the recommendations.
localIntel.use: Recommendation 1.4.9 is the line for any dynamic or moving mattress: NICE says to consider a dynamic support surface when high-specification foam is not enough for someone with a pressure ulcer.

localIntel.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
localIntel.title: Pressure ulcers (QS89)
localIntel.fact: Eight quality statements: risk assessment in hospitals and care homes with nursing, risk assessment by community nursing services, reassessment, skin assessment, advice on repositioning, help with repositioning, information on preventing pressure ulcers, and pressure redistribution devices (statement 8). Statement 9, on medical device-related pressure ulcers, is a placeholder. It applies in England and Wales.
localIntel.use: Statement 8 is the measurable standard a trust's mattress and cushion provision can be audited against.

localIntel.title: Implementing the pressure ulcer framework in local reporting systems and reporting to NRLS
localIntel.date: Not dated on the document (held in NHS England's September 2021 uploads)
localIntel.fact: A guide for tissue viability nurses and pressure ulcer prevention leads on putting the 'Pressure ulcers: revised definition and measurement framework' into local incident reporting. The recommendations it lists include: the Department of Health and Social Care definition of avoidable/unavoidable should not be used; the 72-hour rule should be abandoned; pressure ulcers of grade 2 and above (the guide's wording) present on admission, and unstageable ulcers, should be included in local monitoring; moisture-associated skin damage should be counted alongside. Where pressure-relieving equipment failed or was unavailable but no ulcer occurred, the incident is reported under a separate listing, not as a medical device related pressure ulcer. It is written for the National Reporting and Learning System (NRLS); whether NRLS is still the national route was not verified here.
localIntel.quote: Pressure ulcer categories should not be linked to a specific preset degree of harm
localIntel.use: How a trust counts pressure harm, which is the baseline a business case for a new surface has to move.

localIntel.title: Cohort study evaluating the burden of wounds to the UK's National Health Service in 2017/2018: update from 2012/2013
localIntel.fact: Estimates, from a sample of 3,000 patients' records, 202,000 recorded pressure ulcers in 2017/18, equivalent to 0.4% of the adult population. The annual NHS cost of managing all wounds was £8.3 billion, 81% of it incurred in the community. The healing rate of pressure ulcers was 43% higher, in relative terms, than in 2012/13, and patients with a pressure ulcer had a nursing visit or dressing change every 3 to 4 days. A pressure-ulcer-only cost figure was not checked here.
localIntel.quote: There were an estimated 202 000 recorded pressure ulcers in the study year
localIntel.use: A citable national volume (2017/18) for the cost-of-problem and frequency lines of a value case.

localIntel.org: National Pressure Injury Advisory Panel (NPIAP), European Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel (EPUAP) and Pan Pacific Pressure Injury Alliance (PPPIA)
localIntel.title: Prevention and Treatment of Pressure Ulcers/Injuries: Clinical Practice Guideline (online edition)
localIntel.date: Quick Reference Guide marked final version September 2026
localIntel.ends: Online guideline in Beta mode, regularly updated
localIntel.fact: The online guideline is in Beta mode; the site says it regularly updates content and functionality. It has chapters on repositioning and mobilisation, full body support surfaces, pressure injuries in seated individuals, and technologies to assess skin and tissue. The Quick Reference Guide is marked as the final version of September 2026. Over 200 contributors from more than 40 countries.
localIntel.quote: The online guideline is in Beta mode.
localIntel.use: The support surfaces and repositioning chapters are the evidence base any powered or moving surface claim will be tested against.

localIntel.title: Prevention and management of pressure ulcers standards
localIntel.fact: Apply across health and social care in Scotland to anyone at risk of, or with, a pressure ulcer, including primary and secondary care, hospices, independent clinics, care at home and care homes. The standards cover organisational leadership, staff education and training, information for people, initial risk assessment at admission or first contact, regular reassessment and a person-centred care plan.
localIntel.quote: An initial risk assessment is undertaken as part of admission to, or first contact with, a care service to inform care planning.
localIntel.use: Scotland's counterpart to NICE QS89, and it reaches care at home and care homes.
